transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-31 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: (auto) | Attendees: Lena Ortiz, Samir Patel (Redwood) — Maya Thompson, Omar Ruiz, Priya Desai (Orchid)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we can kick off — i'm lena, account exec at Redwood Inference. happy to run through how customers typically integrate, and samir will chime in on the technical pieces.
[00:15] Maya Thompson: thanks lena. quick context — Orchid Logistics runs route optimization and customer support bots. we're evaluating LLM infra for both in-app chat and batch summarization. primary concerns: latency for chat, cost for batch, and security requirements for PII.
[00:32] Lena Ortiz: got it. at a high level we offer hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, or private deploy in your VPC / on-prem. most teams start hosted for speed then move to dedicated when they need predictable throughput or data separation.
[00:48] Samir Patel: yeah and from an integration perspective we have SDKs for python and node, plus direct REST. we also provide example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex — though sometimes the names are transcribed oddly in docs, it's basically sample chains and retriever patterns.
[01:05] Omar Ruiz: can you share an example of a LangChain flow? we use LangChain heavily and also have a search index built on Elastic.
[01:20] Samir Patel: sure — we have a repo with a LangChain llm wrapper that shows streaming, function-calling, and token-aware retry. it includes code for LlamaIndex too. I'll attach the link after. it's important to size the batch and kv cache settings based on your seq lengths.
[01:38] Priya Desai: on deployment: our security team prefers private or at least VPC peering. what does 'private' actually mean here? data plane in our VPC?
[01:50] Lena Ortiz: private means the control plane runs in Redwood but the inference nodes are in your VPC or on-prem. you control networking and KMS for encryption-at-rest if desired. for strict compliance we also offer a fully air-gapped on-prem option.
[02:07] Maya Thompson: any SOC2 documentation? and does the dedicated option have separate logging?
[02:15] Lena Ortiz: yes SOC2 and we can provide an attestation. dedicated has tenant isolation and logs per customer, and you get audit logs with per-token traces in the console.
[02:28] Omar Ruiz: speaking of logs, how do we integrate observability? we use Datadog + OpenTelemetry.
[02:36] Samir Patel: we emit per-request trace IDs and support exporting metrics via Prometheus / OpenTelemetry. you can attach hooks so each request in your gateway includes our trace id as a header, and the console provides per-route latency and cost breakdowns.
[02:52] Maya Thompson: good. our infra currently has a central gateway that forwards LLM calls. would you recommend a sidecar per service or a central proxy?
[03:04] Samir Patel: it depends. central gateway is fine for uniform policy enforcement and caching, but sidecars can reduce cross-service latency and enable local prefix caching. Redwood's routing can be used either way — we support a proxy/gateway pattern and also sidecar SDKs.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: and we have rate-limit and quota controls on both the control plane and at the SDK level; for high-throughput customers we recommend dedicated pools with burst capacity.
[03:32] Omar Ruiz: what's the typical latency difference between hosted and dedicated?
[03:40] Samir Patel: hosted is optimized for general workloads, median token latency around 60-120ms depending on model and seq length. dedicated on reserved GPUs often gets you consistent lower tail latencies — think 30-80ms — because you control capacity and batching is tuned. numbers vary by model.
[03:58] Priya Desai: cost is big for us. batch summarization runs a lot at night. does Redwood support asynchronous batch APIs or pricing for batch jobs?
[04:08] Lena Ortiz: yes, we have a batch API pattern and also recommend quantized model variants for cheaper batch. Redwood Optimize can give recommendations on batching and quantization to lower token cost.
[04:19] Maya Thompson: about SDKs: do you have official Python examples that plug into LlamaIndex? I saw a community snippet but need production-ready code.
[04:29] Samir Patel: yes, we have an official LlamaIndex connector and documented patterns for embeddings + retriever setup. note: sometimes in auto transcripts 'LlamaIndex' is spelled odd, but the repo is current. I'll share links and a short sample in the follow-up.
[04:44] Omar Ruiz: rate limits — we have spikes during dispatch windows. can you do quota bursting?
[04:51] Samir Patel: we support burst capacity with Dedicated and can configure autoscale policies. for hosted customers we have quota tiers; you can request rate limit increases and we do negotiated burst windows for enterprise plans.
[05:08] Priya Desai: what about request size limits and token caps? we have some prompts that are long (8-12k tokens).
[05:16] Samir Patel: our runtime supports longer context models; we have pipeline recommendations when you hit >8k tokens — chunking + retrieval or KV caching. there are soft token caps per model and hard caps at the hardware/kernel level. we'll quantify model-specific limits in the doc.
[05:32] Maya Thompson: observability hooks again — will tracing span through our proxy into Redwood so we can correlate?
[05:40] Samir Patel: yes, pass our trace id header and you can correlate spans in your APM. we also provide span metadata in the audit logs for each request (model, tokens in/out, latency).
[05:54] Lena Ortiz: can we talk briefly about the onboarding timeline? what does a PoC look like?
[06:02] Samir Patel: a typical PoC: week 0 discovery, week 1 sandbox sign-up + sample integration (LangChain demo), week 2 run benchmarks with your sample payloads, week 3 tune batching/quantization and review cost/latency tradeoffs. Dedicated provisioning adds lead time — typically 2–4 weeks depending on capacity.
[06:24] Omar Ruiz: provisioning for private deploy — how long for VPC/private control plane?
[06:30] Lena Ortiz: VPC deploys are usually 1–2 weeks for simple setups; fully on-prem provisioning longer, depends on installation window and security review.
[06:40] Maya Thompson: a few security questions — KMS integration and key rotation, and SSO for our users.
[06:47] Samir Patel: we integrate with customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest and you can rotate keys per your schedule. SSO via SAML/SSO/OIDC is supported for the console and APIs. we'll include a security pack with the integration guide.
[07:02] Priya Desai: any gotchas with LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors and long-running sessions? we worry about KV cache eviction.
[07:10] Samir Patel: eviction policies are configurable; we surface cache hit rates in the console. for long-running sessions you'll want to pin KV caches to a session id or use our persistent cache storage in Dedicated.
[07:26] Maya Thompson: do you have examples of gateway header patterns and auth flow? we use an internal token exchange.
[07:35] Samir Patel: yes — header patterns: x-redwood-trace-id, x-redwood-request-id, and bearer tokens. for private installs we support mTLS between gateway and inference nodes.
[07:50] Lena Ortiz: any competitors you're actively evaluating?
[07:52] Priya Desai: we've looked at Anthropic for chat and also using OpenAI for prototyping; internal teams also considered hosting on SageMaker endpoints.
[07:59] Lena Ortiz: good to know — we can include a comparison doc but we'll focus on integration velocity and predictable economics.
[08:08] Omar Ruiz: what kind of observability retention do you provide — logs and metrics retention windows?
[08:15] Samir Patel: default is 30 days for detailed traces and 90 days for aggregated metrics; enterprise packages allow longer retention and S3 export of logs.
[08:26] Maya Thompson: ok what about throttling behavior — if we exceed a quota, do you queue, drop, or return 429s?
[08:33] Samir Patel: by default we return 429s for rate-limited requests; with Dedicated we can provision queueing and customizable backpressure strategies.
[08:45] Priya Desai: any offline/batch integrations for large nightly jobs? we may want to call quantized models offline.
[08:52] Samir Patel: yes batch API, and you can run jobs on cheaper quantized variants. we also support async webhooks for job completion.
[09:02] Omar Ruiz: sample payloads — what's most helpful for you to benchmark?
[09:08] Samir Patel: request logs for a week with sizes, seq length, embedding dims, and concurrency patterns. ideally a csv or sample traces.
[09:16] Maya Thompson: we can provide that.
[09:18] Lena Ortiz: next steps recap — we'll send pricing + security pack, samir will schedule a tech demo and ask for sample payloads.
[09:26] Priya Desai: timeline: we aim to pick a PoC by mid-April.
[09:31] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. i'll send the packs by Friday. samir, do you want to propose demo slots?
[09:36] Samir Patel: yes i'll follow up with 2 slots next week and a short agenda focusing on LangChain + LlamaIndex integration and a live benchmark.
[09:46] Maya Thompson: small nit — in your docs, do you address tenant-level cost attribution? we need per-product billing for internal chargeback.
[09:54] Lena Ortiz: yes the console provides token-level cost breakdown and you can split by route/service; we can export granular CSVs for chargeback.
[10:06] Omar Ruiz: any limits on the number of routes we can create?
[10:10] Samir Patel: no hard limit; we recommend grouping logically but the platform supports many routes and per-route SLOs.
[10:22] Priya Desai: okay that covers most. thanks everyone.
[10:25] Lena Ortiz: thanks — we'll follow up with the docs and demo invite. meeting end.
